data.exact_reserve_text:
There have been adverse movements on all underwriting years, apart from on 2007 where a release of claims reserves has resulted in an underwriting profit of GBP 8.3m on that year.

Due to the continuing uncertainty on the Italian Public Hospital Medical Malpractice reserves the Board of the Managing Agent has resolved to leave the 2007 year of account open. The Syndicate ceased underwriting this business from the 2008 year of account. However, the uncertainty over the ultimate cost of Italian Public Hospitals claims has reduced and a reserve release on the 2007 and prior years of account has resulted in an operating profit of GBP 8,334k for the financial year.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Uncertainty over ultimate cost reduced leading to a reserve release on the 2007 and prior years of account resulting in an operating profit of GBP 8,334k for the financial year.

data.standardized_narrative: At 31 December 2015 the Syndicate's gross claims outstanding closed at GBP 551.198m (opening balance at 1 Jan 2015: GBP 549.509m). The report states there were adverse movements across most underwriting years, with the exception of a reserve release on the 2007 year (linked to Italian Public Hospitals medical malpractice) which produced an underwriting profit of GBP 8.334m. The statement does not provide a single explicit GROSS total for prior-year development; narrative references a targeted release on 2007 and otherwise adverse development across other years.

data.data_quality_notes: No explicit single gross 'movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' figure was located in the notes. Narrative identifies a reserve release on the 2007 year (Italian Public Hospitals) and states generally adverse movements on other years. A gross claims development triangle is present but OCR/extraction ambiguity and an aggregate 'Before 2011' column make a reliable gross PYD calculation uncertain; therefore prior_year_development_gbp_m is returned as null. If a gross PYD is required, manual review of the claims development table (page 35) is recommended.
